picks.rationale: Ludo.ai's Keyframe Animation turns one-shot generative sprites into art-directable frames — a concrete tool change a 2D game artist can act on tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: Ludo.ai has launched Keyframe Animation, a tool giving game developers direct control over AI-generated sprite animations, alongside new 3D asset tooling. It pushes generative art from one-shot output toward editable, art-directable frames.

picks.rationale: Horii defends shipping Slimey, a conversational AI companion, inside Dragon Quest — a named designer putting his reputation behind an AI NPC as an accessibility layer rather than a labour cut.
picks.excerpt: Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii says AI 'hardly ever makes things up' anymore and defends building the conversational companion Slimey into the series, arguing it 'lowers the barrier of entry to interacting with AI.'

picks.rationale: A shipped production case, not a demo: a non-technical designer worked directly in the codebase via an AI assistant and cut a five-to-six week feature to two.
picks.excerpt: Dark and Darker studio IRONMACE describes how AI coding assistant Aura let a non-technical designer work directly in the codebase to prototype and ship the game's new tutorial — a job the studio estimates would normally have taken five to six weeks, done in two.

picks.rationale: Sega narrowing its Steam AI disclosure to ideation-only and pledging to strip AI-derived content before release turns disclosure language into a production commitment studios will be held to.
picks.excerpt: Sega rewrote Crazy Taxi: World Tour's Steam AI disclosure to say generative AI was used only for ideation on background objects — and that all AI-derived content will be removed before release. A concrete case of disclosure language becoming a production commitment.

picks.rationale: A shipped character-AI product with an explicit consent model — no training on chat logs, voice built only from the original actor's clips — sets a workable precedent for licensed AI companions.
picks.excerpt: Atelier has turned Ryza into RyzaChat: AI, an open-ended chatbot companion app on iOS and Android in Japan. The team frames it as an 'ethical AI adventure' — no chat logs used for training, and a voice trained only on the original Japanese actor's clips.
